864 organizations sent nearly 1,800 letters of interest in Alaska's $272,174,856 rural health program.

The Department of Health invited 403 of them to apply. On August 7th the first Friday of a weekly series funded nineteen projects, $4.5 million in all. That is less than 2 percent of the first year allocation.

Chugachmiut got $627,200 for portable X-ray machines in five rural clinics. The Nenana Volunteer Fire Department received $50,000 to plan a new mobile crisis team. Kodiak, the Yukon-Kuskokwim Delta and the North Slope have nothing in round one.

The state's own words on drones and AI-enabled tools sit next to five awards named with amounts plus fourteen that published reporting doesn't itemise.

What should a Friday list say about a project besides its name and its amount?

#RuralHealthTransformation #AlaskaHealthPolicy #HealthTechProcurement

Editor's note

SHIP. 8.91 against a threshold of 7.7 at revision round 4, and it also clears the unrelaxed 8.3, so there is no shortfall to flag. Zero hard fails on a from-scratch re-run of all thirteen. THE PRIOR HARD FAIL IS DEAD: slide 06's kicker reads FOURTEEN MORE IT DOES NOT in the HTML, in copy.json and in the pixels, no slide string in the deck opens with And or But, and the sentence still runs across the cut from slide 05. On the T2 amendment, judged plainly: the slide 06 half is honest and accepted; the slide 07 half is a small, disclosed goalpost move that survives on substance, and the next deck should author Device B with the object-versus-geography distinction in it from the start rather than inherit an amendment. The weakest criterion is the caption's posture: it recites the record and never states the deck's own thesis. The deck's tightest contrast pair is slide 06's honesty note over the lit trench front; it reads, but it is the first place to look if anyone reports a legibility complaint. The caption_check date-form inconsistency this run self-reported is real, and the run complied with the gate rather than the doc, which was the right call.

Story reframed from the briefed headline. The fact-checker killed 'the fund bought no autonomy' (the state publishes the nineteen-project list only as an unparseable spreadsheet) and killed the Alaska Native Language Center candidate outright (the AI link is manufactured, the August 11th article never mentions AI). What shipped is the menu-versus-order frame, which is provable from two primary documents. Slide 06 is the honesty firewall and it is drawn at full weight rather than hidden. One live inconsistency for the machine to settle: caption_check's DATE table has no year exemption, so it rejects 'October 30, 2026' although brand.yaml and CAPTION_CRAFT both permit the plain form when a year is present. This run complied by writing the ordinal on slides 08 and 09; the gate and the docs still disagree.

The routine modified its own machinery this run. If a later week looks worse, this dated section is the rollback trail (each set reverts as one commit).

fix
scripts		THE ON-SLIDE TEXT RULES NOW RUN ON ON-SLIDE TEXT. Two changes to caption_check.py, one shape and one rule. (1) copy_prose() walked a slide only when its value was a DICT, so a copy.json whose slides are LISTS OF STRINGS -- the shape the copy room actually writes -- contributed nothing at all, and this run reported copy_fields_checked 4, the caption-side prose fields only. It now recurses through dicts, lists and nested lists, so the date table and the banned-phrase pass finally reach the strings set in type on the artwork: 4 fields checked became 47 on this run's own copy.json. (2) New check_slide_openers() enforces brand.yaml's 'No slide string opens with And or But' (maintainer, 2026-08-05), which was written twice in config/brand.yaml and had no code anywhere. Editor-only fields (editor_notes_for_email, aftercare, caption_meta) stay out of scope exactly as before, and only the HEAD of a slide string is tested, because the rule is about opening.

A slide whose artwork carries a number in a POSITION declares <body data-scale> with from/to as [design px, value], the band the scale owns, and every mark in that band with what it means. qa.py FAILs a mark that declares no meaning, a mark outside its own span, and any run of ink in the band, at least as strong as the weakest mark the slide itself declared, that the slide does not declare, printing the VALUE that position reads as. Aftercare (this is where reach is won)

  • Post as a document (PDF) so LinkedIn renders all nine pages, not as nine images.
  • Set the document title to 'The Menu and the First Friday' on upload. A document post has no alt text, so the caption is the whole deck for a screen reader.
  • Paste the first comment within 60 seconds of posting. The post body carries no links by house rule.
  • The five itemised awards are the only ones published reporting names. If a reader asks what the other fourteen bought, the honest answer is that the record does not say yet.
  • October 30th, 2026 is the end of the first budget period. Never call it an obligation deadline.
  • The Norton Sound scheduling system is never described as AI. No source calls it that.
  • Decisions release each Friday, so this story has a next instalment. Watch for the following Friday's list.
